One of my favorite poems, "O Me! O Life!", by Walt Whitman sums it up nicely...

Oh me! Oh life! of the questions of these recurring,

Of the endless trains of the faithless, of cities fill’d with the foolish,

Of myself forever reproaching myself, (for who more foolish than I, and who more faithless?)

Of eyes that vainly crave the light, of the objects mean, of the struggle ever renew’d,

Of the poor results of all, of the plodding and sordid crowds I see around me,

Of the empty and useless years of the rest, with the rest me intertwined,

The question, O me! so sad, recurring—What good amid these, O me, O life?

Answer.

That you are here—that life exists and identity,

That the powerful play goes on, and you may contribute a verse.

I think what this is is the conflation of "atheism" with a particular (and all too common) shallow form of materialism. And as far as that goes, there is some basis for the conflation, since it's a relatively common paired set of presumptions. It's not, however, universal, or likely even close to it.

What I mean by that - there really are a great number of people with a shallow and superficial understanding of philosophy who do in fact believe that there is no "God" and that there is no "meaning," and often do link those beliefs. What they actually believe though, although they're generally either too dull-witted and/or reactionary to understand it, is that there is no objective meaning, without even beginning to understand that "meaning" doesn't need to be objective in order to have... well... meaning. They're shallow materialists and they apparently sincerely believe - or at least often claim to believe - that a thing that doesn't have a material existence flatly "doesn't exist," apparently entirely unaware of the fact that that means that every thought they've ever had, including that one, "doesn't exist." They seem entirely unable to distinguish between "existence" as it pertains to material objects and "existence" as it pertains to concepts, and thus unable to grasp the fact that while concepts don't "exist" in the same sense that material objects "exist," they DO in fact "exist" as much as they need to in order to be what they in fact are.

Regarding "meaning" - as soon as an individual attaches it to something, it "exists" exactly as much as it needs to, and that in spite of the fact that you'll never be able to isolate it and observe it and measure it. All too many shallow materialists just don't seem to grasp that.

Additionally, the conflation is generally made, as it seems to be in this case, by theists who labor under a somewhat similar delusion. In parallel with that same misconception that "meaning" must be objective, they have an all too common misconception that somehow "God says so" makes something objective, which is how they come to believe that someone who doesn't believe in "God" can't find any meaning in life. They don't realize that the meaning they take from their faith is ultimately just as subjective as the meaning anyone else takes from any other source - no more and no less. So it's not that they have a basis for their meaning and other people don't - other people just have different bases for their meaning.
